name: Black feminism
summary: Black feminism holds that Black women face racism, sexism and class exploitation as one interlocking system, so neither the mainstream feminist nor the Black liberation movement serves them unless they address all three together. Its mainstream, as in the Combahee River Collective, is socialist and anti-imperialist, supports reproductive rights and opposes state violence and incarceration. It values Black women's own self-definition and knowledge as a base for politics.
scope: The US Black feminist tradition from the 1970s on: the Combahee River Collective Statement (1977), Kimberle Crenshaw's intersectionality, Patricia Hill Collins's Black Feminist Thought and Angela Davis's abolitionist and socialist writing, with earlier figures such as Harper, Wells and Chisholm in the background. Economic and foreign-policy answers lean on the Combahee socialist strand and Davis and are mostly low confidence; liberal and religious womanist strands would answer some of them more moderately.

keyFigures.name: Kimberle Crenshaw
keyFigures.role: Coined 'intersectionality' in 1989 to describe the compounded discrimination Black women face.

keyFigures.name: Patricia Hill Collins
keyFigures.role: Author of Black Feminist Thought and the 'matrix of domination' framework.

keyFigures.name: Angela Davis
keyFigures.role: Marxist scholar and activist, author of Women, Race and Class and leading prison abolitionist.

sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Standpoint, controlling images, self-definition and intellectual activism.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Combahee's projects included health care and its socialism calls for resources distributed to those who create them, so a state guarantee of care fits.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Black women's long, harsher economic exploitation (Beale) makes wage floors a natural demand, though the sources do not discuss the minimum wage itself.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The Collective calls for destroying capitalism and organising work for collective benefit, which is incompatible with trusting free markets.

public-ownership.rationale: Collective benefit of those who do the work implies non-capitalist ownership, but the statement does not specify state ownership of utilities.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Equal distribution of material resources to those who create them implies steeply redistributive taxation.

unions-good.rationale: Worker control of production is endorsed, but the sources discuss unions little and note labour movements' own racism and sexism.

property-fundamental.rationale: Anti-capitalism and collective benefit reject private property as an overriding right.

regulate-corporations.rationale: An anti-capitalist politics favours tighter control of corporations at minimum, as a step short of abolishing capitalism.

cut-welfare.rationale: Collins treats the 'welfare mother' as a controlling image that makes Black women's subordination look natural, so cutting welfare on dependency grounds is rejected.

worker-ownership.rationale: The Combahee statement says work must be organised for the collective benefit of those who do the work.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Davis-style abolitionist and Black Panther politics distrust state security power that has targeted Black activists; terrorism is not discussed.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Prison abolition and critique of mass incarceration point toward ending drug criminalisation, though sources do not address drugs directly.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Adherents are split between wanting protection from racist speech and distrusting state criminal-law tools used against Black people.

strong-leader.rationale: The Collective stresses collective, non-hierarchical leadership and rejects rule by a single strongman; Black women's liberation is framed as from below.

state-harmful.rationale: Abolitionists want police and prisons gone but the mainstream also demands state protection and services, so adherents are split on the state as such.

limit-guns.rationale: Davis's Panther background includes armed self-defence while feminists also stress violence against women; sources show no settled line.

empower-police-military.rationale: Davis advocates abolishing police and prisons and the tradition documents state violence against Black women, so more police power is rejected.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Black feminists split between viewing sex work as exploitation and as labour; the Wikipedia article is silent on it.

decide-locally.rationale: Nothing in the sources puts the level of government as a principle; the demand is for transformed power rather than localisation.

rehabilitation.rationale: Davis's abolitionism holds mass incarceration is a new form of slavery and favours investing in alternatives to punishment.

traditional-family.rationale: Black feminists criticise idealised nuclear-family and housewife models as unfit to Black women's histories, and see family ideology as a vector of patriarchy.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The Collective opposes heterosexual oppression and many members were Black lesbians; marriage as an institution is debated, so support is moderate.

abortion-legal.rationale: Chisholm demanded an end to 'compulsory pregnancy' and Combahee worked on abortion rights and sterilisation abuse.

more-religion-public.rationale: Black feminism has strong church-rooted strands but its political programme is secular and anti-patriarchal; a larger public religious role is not sought.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The Collective's central commitment is struggle against racial oppression, and the tradition criticises racial capitalism from slavery on.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The tradition treats gendered roles and 'controlling images' as socially imposed, though its treatment of gender identity is not uniform.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: A tradition of critiquing US national myths and white male rule disfavours preserving national tradition as such, though Black cultural heritage is valued.

gradual-change.rationale: The Collective describes itself as revolutionary and demands the destruction of interlocking systems, not gradual reform.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not directly addressed; the solidarity and anti-oppression framework and critique of Black nationalism's exclusions imply opposition to restriction.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Davis stresses transnational solidarity, but the sources show no position on UN-style institutions.

free-trade.rationale: Anti-imperialist, anti-capitalist politics distrusts free-trade agreements, though trade is not discussed.

nation-first.rationale: The Collective opposes imperialism and frames liberation as universal, so national self-interest over cooperation is rejected.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Opposition to imperialism makes adherents wary of foreign military intervention, inferred rather than stated.

open-borders.rationale: Internationalist solidarity points that way, but the sources do not state a position on borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Environmental questions are not central to the sources; adherents are split.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Davis attributes disasters like Katrina to racism, capitalism and imperialism, implying support for strong action, but climate policy is not a stated tenet.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Structural-oppression analysis holds that social systems, not technology, are the problem.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed; no inference is possible beyond general scepticism of state-corporate projects.

revolution-justified.rationale: The Collective describes its work as revolutionary and aims at a revolutionary society.

experts-over-public.rationale: Collins's standpoint theory holds that Black women are authors of knowledge about their own lives, which cuts against deference to expert elites.

central-planning.rationale: Socialist, but the statement does not endorse a particular planning mechanism, and Black feminists mostly leave this unspecified.

socialized-markets.rationale: The statement requires collective benefit but is silent on whether markets may survive under collective ownership.

land-value-tax.rationale: No relevant position in the sources.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Redistribution of resources to those who create them implies taxing large inherited wealth; inferred.

basic-income.rationale: Distribution of material resources and welfare defence suggest sympathy, but UBI is not discussed.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Not addressed and the tradition has no stated position.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Not addressed; socialist leanings point one way, distrust of the state the other.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The programme emphasises collective rather than small-owner property.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The Collective is socialist but does not call for abolishing money or wages.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: A market-money anarcho-capitalist demand; nothing in the tradition supports it.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised class-collaboration bodies conflict with the Collective's radical stance, though not discussed.

one-party-rule.rationale: Davis left the Communist Party in 1991 over its backing of the Soviet coup attempt, and feminist politics stresses participatory democracy, so single-party rule is rejected.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Opposition to inherited hierarchy and 'white male rule' makes hereditary monarchy illegitimate; inferred.

democracy-best.rationale: Black feminists criticise American democracy as white male rule but seek inclusion in and expansion of democracy; Harper argued Black women needed the vote.

workers-councils.rationale: Worker control and collective benefit fit councils, but the statement does not endorse councils specifically.

right-to-secede.rationale: Black nationalist secession is discussed but Black feminists criticise nationalism's male dominance and do not endorse secession in general.

natural-rulers.rationale: The tradition rests on rejecting hierarchies of race and sex; the claim that some are naturally fit to rule is contrary to its core.

political-violence-never.rationale: Davis and the Panthers did not renounce violence, but most Black feminist activism emphasises organising; adherents lean away from absolutist pacifism.

war-builds-character.rationale: Anti-imperialism and the critique of patriarchy reject glorifying war.

separate-church-state.rationale: A secular political programme, though Black churches are valued; no explicit statement.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The Collective's programme opposes patriarchal and heterosexist law, which scripture-based legislation typically upholds.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Davis's abolitionism and anti-capitalism reject marketised policing and justice.

military-superiority.rationale: Anti-imperialist politics rejects pursuing military dominance.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Intersectional anti-oppression thinking rejects ethnically defined nations.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The Collective agrees with Marx on the analysis of material economic relations while insisting race and sex shape struggle too.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The statement demands equal distribution of material resources among those who create them.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Anti-colonial, anti-oppression framework suggests support, but not a topic of the sources.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The Collective opposes imperialism; reparations for colonialism are inferred, not stated.

civilizational-union.rationale: Not discussed; a universalist anti-oppression politics is not organised on civilisational lines.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Collective benefit and solidarity are central, and the Collective says everyone must be free.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The emphasis is on rights against oppression and collective liberation rather than on duties to a community that has excluded Black women.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Alice Walker's womanism embraces the solidarity of humanity and the earth, but ecology is not central to the sources.

limit-population.rationale: Davis documented compulsory sterilisation of Black women, so state population limits are rejected as reproductive coercion.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Marxian critique targets capitalism, not industry as such.

accelerate-technology.rationale: No endorsement in sources; disruption for its own sake is not an aim.

human-enhancement.rationale: None of the sources discuss body-modifying technology, so adherents have no common line; neutral, low confidence.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Distrust of unaccountable systems that reproduce racial bias is inferred; not discussed.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Distrust of surveillance of Black activists implies support, inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: The Collective sees the past order as white male rule and seeks a revolutionary new society.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The Collective is an explicitly ideological, analysis-driven politics.

direct-action.rationale: Black feminist organising has mixed activism and electoral/legal work (Chisholm ran for office); direct action is common but not exclusive.

means-match-ends.rationale: The Collective stresses integrated analysis and practice and collective process.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Nothing in the tradition supports it.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The tradition criticises gendered and racial divisions of labour but does not call for total abolition.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Socialist distribution of resources to meet the needs of the most oppressed is the stated goal.

production-for-use.rationale: The statement says work should be organised for collective benefit, not profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The Collective accepts Marx's analysis of economic exploitation and rejects profit-driven work.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The Collective is socialist but critical of male-dominated vanguardist politics; dictatorial rule is not endorsed.

collective-farming.rationale: The Combahee statement and Black feminist sources never address agriculture or land organisation, so no position can be inferred.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Imperialism is named as a system to be destroyed together with capitalism, implying their link.

taxation-theft.rationale: Redistributive politics is the opposite of this claim.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Intersectional analysis focuses on structures and group-based oppression, as in Crenshaw's critique of single-axis legal claims.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Collective political voice and organising are central; exit is not a response to oppression.

state-as-business.rationale: Anti-capitalist politics rejects treating citizens as customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: The Collective ties freedom to material resources distributed to those who create them.

media-academia-power.rationale: Collins documents how media images shape Black women's oppression but the tradition does not claim academia outranks elected power.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The tradition rejects biological race hierarchy as the basis of oppression.

organic-representation.rationale: The tradition seeks representation through Black women's own organisations and movements, not through corporatist families and trade bodies, so this is a mild rejection inferred.

total-state.rationale: Opposition to systemic domination and white male rule means rejecting state direction of all life.

national-rebirth.rationale: The Collective seeks social revolution, not nationalist rebirth.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The Combahee statement names imperialism among the systems whose destruction is necessary, which rules out a nation expanding its territory and influence abroad.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal personal rule conflicts with the Collective's egalitarian aims.

bound-labor.rationale: The tradition's critique of racial capitalism starts from slavery; coerced bound labour is condemned.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Collins's standpoint theory holds Black women author knowledge from their position and that dominant knowledge reflects power.

universal-morality.rationale: Collins's epistemology stresses situated knowledge, yet the movement also appeals to universal human worth; split.

single-common-good.rationale: Intersectionality holds that supposedly universal single-axis approaches marginalise those with multiple identities, so one common good is suspect.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Davis supports BDS against Israel, though the question is not central to Black feminism as a whole.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora return rights are a nationalist question that the sources on Black feminism do not take up, so neutral.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is a nationalist concern absent from the Black feminist sources used here, so neutral.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Workers organised and controlling their labour for collective benefit entails democratic voice at work.

school-vouchers.rationale: Public provision is generally favoured by the left; vouchers are not discussed.

economic-freedom.rationale: Treats freedom as resting on material means, not market freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Not endorsed; the tradition demands structural change.

national-self-determination.rationale: Opposition to imperialism implies support, though the statement does not discuss nations.

force-without-un.rationale: Anti-imperialism leads adherents to oppose unilateral force; inferred.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Collins values poetry, music and lived experience as knowledge, and Black church traditions are respected; rationalism as sole guide is not held.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Solidarity politics and marginalisation analysis oppose excluding immigrants; inferred.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Collins's controlling image of the 'welfare mother' and Roberts's work on punishing Black mothers inform opposition to punitive work requirements.

class-collaboration.rationale: The Collective analyses class oppression and demands worker control, not partnership with employers.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Collins's work reclaims suppressed Black women's intellectual and cultural heritage, so sacrificing cultural institutions is opposed.

dominated-front.rationale: Third-world solidarity is plausible given Davis, but not documented.

workers-nation.rationale: The Collective's liberation project is international in scope, aimed at destroying capitalism and imperialism, not at national working-class blocs.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Black feminism rejects the idea of distinct public roles by sex; Pauli Murray fought sex discrimination alongside civil rights.

ban-interest.rationale: Usury bans appear nowhere in the sources; the socialist critique targets profit and exploitation, so only a slight inferred rejection of a legal ban.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Struggle against racial oppression is central.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Collective calls US politics a system of white male rule and sees class oppression as a core system, though it does not state a theory of the state.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Davis blamed capitalism and imperialism for disasters such as Katrina; environmental justice leanings oppose expansion, but energy policy is not stated.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Intersectional politics values the cultures and self-definition of marginalised groups rather than demanding assimilation.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory targeting immigrants and minorities, contrary to the anti-oppression framework.

proportional-representation.rationale: Inclusion of marginalised groups in politics favours proportional systems, but electoral systems are not discussed.

national-mission.rationale: Anti-imperialism rejects exporting a national model by mission.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The Collective names sexual oppression as a system and calls US politics a system of white male rule.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Black feminism describes political power as white male rule insulated from Black women, but corruption is not the stated frame.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Davis and Roberts document compulsory sterilisation of Black women, which this eugenic policy would repeat.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Black feminist activism addressed state and sexual violence against Black women (Recy Taylor, Rosa Lee Ingram), implying accountability for abuses.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Socialist redistribution and collective benefit are contrary to a minimal state.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Collective's demand that Black women be recognised as of equal worth, and its stress on equal inclusion, rest on this principle.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The statement is internationalist but does not address socialist-state theory.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Anti-colonial and anti-oppression frameworks lean this way, though the sources do not state it.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Religious personal law versus a common code is not a topic in the Black feminist sources, so neutral.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Opposition to coercive control over personal belief.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Inferred from a secular programme, with church-rooted traditions leaving some split.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Davis left the Communist Party in 1991 and the feminist tradition distrusts strengthened coercive states.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Harper's argument that Black women needed the vote implies legitimate power depends on the participation of the governed.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist export targets are not discussed by Black feminist writers, so no position is documented.

population-transfer.rationale: State coercion over minority populations is condemned; Roberts and Davis document such abuses against Black women.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The tradition accepts that violence by the state and in self-defence is political, rather than holding an absolute libertarian rule.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Collective benefit and solidarity are central and the Collective opposes competition-based capitalism.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Davis herself was persecuted as a Communist, making adherents wary of banning parties.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The Collective's aim is the destruction of systems of domination, and its freedom claim is that no one is free while Black women are not.

separated-powers.rationale: The sources criticise US politics as white male rule but offer no theory of checks and balances, so neutral.

vanguard-party.rationale: The Collective stressed collective, grassroots organising and criticised male-dominated movements, and Davis left the CPUSA over its leadership.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The statement aims for a society meeting the needs of the most oppressed.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing tenure policy is not addressed in the sources; redistributive instincts and worries about privatisation pull in opposite directions.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Worker control of production implies defending strike rights.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The tradition ascribes poverty to racial capitalism and structural oppression, and condemns population-control narratives.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Contradicts the tradition's view of difference and solidarity across lines.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is not discussed in the Black feminist sources, so neutral.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Davis was prosecuted by the state and Black activists were targeted by emergency powers; adherents distrust suspension of protections.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Consistent with distribution to need; inferred.

party-controls-media.rationale: Collins emphasises self-definition and Black women's voices against controlling images; state control of media contradicts it.

party-commands-army.rationale: No endorsement; the Collective is critical of centralised party control.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Consistent with equality of resources; inferred.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The Collective stressed collective process and criticised male-dominated organisational hierarchies.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Supranational unions are not discussed; anti-imperial caution and internationalist solidarity pull in opposite directions.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Black church traditions are mixed in polity and the question is not part of the politics.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule by religious scholars is contrary to its egalitarian, anti-patriarchal programme.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Anti-imperialist politics suggests opposing the government's war, but not a stated tenet.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Collins treats poetry, fiction and music as valid Black women's thought; moral censorship would suppress it.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits are not discussed by the sources; a mild inferred wariness of entrenched rulers.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Anti-imperialism suggests ending military alliances and overseas deployments; inferred.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Compulsory home ownership is not part of the Collective's collective-benefit programme, so a mild inferred rejection.

people-in-arms.rationale: Davis's Panther affiliation includes armed self-defence, but the broader tradition has no policy on citizen armies.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National reunification is a nationalist question not covered by the Black feminist sources, so neutral.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Collins valorises Black women's intellectual work, and the tradition itself is academic and activist.

death-penalty.rationale: Davis is a leading abolitionist of prisons and punishment, and the tradition opposes state killing, given racial disparities.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Reproductive rights and bodily autonomy are central to the tradition.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from standpoint on science education.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Black feminists divide on pornography; the sources do not state a line.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Inclusion-oriented politics favours birthright citizenship; inferred.

minority-language-support.rationale: Inclusion of marginalised groups suggests support.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not addressed; tension between religious liberty and anti-discrimination.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Self-definition and acceptance of Black lesbians against norms point to support; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Davis connects capitalism and imperialism to global injustice, implying cancellation; inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Collective holds political change without destroying capitalism and imperialism is inadequate.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitution-writing procedure is not discussed in the sources, so neutral.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The Collective seeks liberation, not sacrifice of freedom for development.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Redistribution and anti-imperialism imply a duty, though aid specifically is not discussed.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Anti-militarism and anti-imperialism oppose national nuclear weapons.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The mode of electing the head of state is not discussed in the sources, so neutral.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Anti-capitalist leanings reject insulating finance from democratic control; inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Davis supports Palestinian solidarity, implying peace over territorial claims; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Work and resources are to be organised for collective benefit.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Davis praised Soviet anti-racism for years and left the CPUSA only in 1991; adherents are split.

collective-defense.rationale: Opposition to military alliances inferred from anti-imperialism.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Solidarity with Palestinians suggests this view; inferred.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Black church is a central community institution and the tradition does not call for curbing it.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: A ceremonial head of state is not a topic in the sources on Black feminism, so neutral.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Anti-imperial stance suggests reluctance to use force against peoples.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Regional autonomy arrangements are not addressed by the sources, so neutral.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Equal distribution of resources demands progressive taxation.

character-from-environment.rationale: The tradition holds identity and outcomes are formed by social structures and conditions, not innate hierarchies.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Collective names white male rule as the problem; unaccountable rulers are rejected.

space-expansion.rationale: Not a priority; resources are needed for human needs; inferred.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Not endorsed; rule by the few conflicts with the tradition.

equal-parenting.rationale: Not addressed; Black feminist views are split.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Davis left the CPUSA over the Soviet coup but no stated theory.

land-redistribution.rationale: Redistribution of resources to those who create them; inferred.

refugee-return.rationale: Davis's solidarity with Palestinians suggests support; inferred.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Opposed to imperialism and ethnic nationalism.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Contradicts egalitarian aims and freedom of belief.

women-must-cover.rationale: Opposes state control of women's bodies and dress.

common-currency.rationale: Currency union is not addressed by the sources, so neutral.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Not addressed; pan-African solidarity exists in the broader tradition but this is not documented in the sources.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority cultural autonomy within states is not discussed in these sources, so neutral despite sympathy for self-definition.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The Collective fights for rights in the US rather than emigration; Black women demand equal inclusion where they live.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The Collective agrees with Marx's theory of material economic relationships but adds race and sex as forces.

ban-cartels.rationale: Not addressed; anti-capitalist politics aims beyond competition policy.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not addressed; anti-capitalism and pro-welfare views pull in opposite directions.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Crenshaw's work shows how courts failing to protect Black women's rights matters, and majorities have marginalised them; protecting minorities from majority is central.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The tradition demands representation of women and Black women in political bodies; Chisholm was a pioneer.

moral-incentives.rationale: The Collective wants work organised for collective benefit but does not discuss moral versus material incentives, so neutral.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The Collective stresses mass organising and collective politics rather than foquismo.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Opposition to inherited systems of dominance is core.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Standpoint critique of dominant narratives opposes a national-centred curriculum.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Imperialism is a system to be destroyed.

patriotic-education.rationale: The Collective calls US politics a system of white male rule and would resist mandated loyalty.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Opposition to racial oppression leads to support for remedial preferences, though the sources do not discuss affirmative action.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary institutions are not discussed by the sources, so neutral.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The Collective holds capitalism must be destroyed, implying it does not simply resolve its crises.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The Collective names imperialism as a system to be destroyed, which implies opposing a former empire's cultivated influence over ex-colonies.

delink-world-market.rationale: The sources condemn imperialism but do not discuss delinking from world trade, so neutral.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Not addressed; Beale's analysis notes white women's middle-class position but not worker exploitation in rich countries.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Crenshaw's work and civil-rights tradition demand legal protection against discrimination.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Protection against majority marginalisation suggests support; inferred.

elective-rulers.rationale: Black feminists fought for suffrage and office-holding (Chisholm), implying elected rulers.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Davis and civil-rights tradition accept resistance to oppressive government; inferred.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Parliamentary versus monarchical supremacy is not discussed in the sources, so neutral.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Walker's womanism extends solidarity beyond humans, though this is not mainstream.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is not discussed by the Black feminist sources, so neutral.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The Collective demands redistribution as right of those who create value, not charity of the privileged.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The Collective is an activist organisation holding that politics grows out of identity and struggle.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Collins describes controlling images like the mammy and jezebel as media stereotypes that make subordination seem natural.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Collins's hegemonic domain of the matrix of domination covers culture and ideology as sustaining power.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Black feminism shares with Black nationalism a critique of racial capitalism, and Davis blames imperialism for global inequality.

party-own-road.rationale: The Collective did not address relations between national communist parties; Davis left the CPUSA over its stance on the Soviet coup, but no line follows.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development strategy for poor countries is not discussed in the sources, so neutral.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; tension with equal-citizenship ideals.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Opposed to white male rule; inferred.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Davis was a communist for decades and the tradition leans socialist; adherents reject equivalence.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: The tradition's critique of racial capitalism begins with slavery and rejects denial of it.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Anti-racist politics generally favours removing monuments honouring slaveholders; not stated.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The tradition prioritises women's disadvantage and the Collective notes Black men may not accept women's equal worth, though male hardship is not denied.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Black feminist activism focused on male violence against women, from Recy Taylor to 1990s campaigns against domestic violence.

paid-care-work.rationale: Black women's long dual labour at home and at work is documented, supporting recognition of domestic work as labour.

filial-duty.rationale: Filial obligations are not discussed in the sources, and the family critique cuts both ways, so neutral.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil-service examinations are not discussed by the sources, so neutral.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Controls on foreign purchases of strategic firms are not discussed, so neutral.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Autonomy for women over marriage; inferred.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Collective provision is preferred to privatised accounts.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land tenure by use is not addressed in the sources, so neutral.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliamentary budget approval is not discussed in the sources, so neutral.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Foreign ownership of land is not discussed in the sources, so neutral.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Crenshaw's work in DeGraffenreid v. General Motors argued courts overlooked compound discrimination by looking only at intent or single axes.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Production for use rather than profit; inferred.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Anti-imperialism opposes covert intervention by the US.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Anti-imperialist politics rejects great-power invasions of allies.

corporate-influence.rationale: Anti-capitalist politics sees corporate power over politics as a central problem.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Davis and Roberts show state reproductive policy has been used to control Black women's bodies, so state population engineering is distrusted.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from opposition to exclusion.

job-guarantee.rationale: Equal distribution of resources and the history of Black women's labour imply support, but it is not a stated demand.

democratic-peace.rationale: The sources criticise US war-making and imperialism but do not assess democratic-peace theory, so neutral.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Davis's abolitionist and civil-rights tradition holds unjust law carries no automatic claim.

non-intervention.rationale: Anti-imperialist but not strictly non-interventionist; solidarity politics is selective.

industrial-unions.rationale: The sources endorse worker control but do not compare industrial and craft unionism, so neutral.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy claims against minorities contradict an anti-oppression framework.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Marriage is critiqued as patriarchal institution but Black lesbians also sought its benefits; split.

local-production.rationale: Localist production is not part of the Black feminist programme in the sources, so neutral.

informal-organisation.rationale: The Collective was a small autonomous group but did not reject parties and unions generally.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Not discussed; internationalist solidarity leads away from it.

religious-nation.rationale: Opposition to exclusionary hierarchies rejects defining nationhood by religion.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Standard socialist position; the statement's collective ownership focus concerns production, though personal property is not discussed.

defeat-communism.rationale: Davis was a Communist Party member for decades and the Collective is socialist.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Delivery mix within publicly funded services is not discussed, so neutral.

religion-illusion.rationale: The tradition includes religious womanist and church-rooted strands and does not treat religion as an illusion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The tradition's critique of racial capitalism begins with slavery rather than crediting capitalism with progress.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Collective says liberation requires destroying capitalism and imperialism along with patriarchy.

socialized-care.rationale: Black women's economic necessity of working outside the home is documented; public provision of care is plausible but not stated.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Linguistic purism has no place in a politics built on self-definition and inclusion, so a mild inferred rejection.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Small self-governing communes are not discussed in the sources, though collective ownership is sympathetic; neutral.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The Collective's answer is socialism, not a third way.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The Black feminist sources take no side on competing historical land claims, so neutral.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The Collective opposes heterosexual oppression and counted Black lesbians among its core.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Davis's own persecution and the Collective's opposition to domination weigh strongly against suppression.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The Collective's call to destroy imperialism opposes governing overseas territories for the ruling country's economic benefit, a defining feature of colonial rule.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Religious-law doctrine unconnected to the tradition.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Not part of the tradition and contrary to its aims.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The Collective stresses collective and bottom-up politics and Black women's own self-definition; participatory democracy is a natural fit.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Crenshaw coined intersectionality and Combahee states its task as integrated analysis of interlocking oppressions.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Black feminism generally supports anti-discrimination protection, but the sources do not address trans issues specifically.

assisted-dying.rationale: Assisted dying is not discussed by Black feminist sources, and adherents are likely split, so neutral.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The Collective is explicitly socialist and locates itself within a left analysis.

alienated-labor.rationale: The Collective accepts Marx's analysis of workers' relationship to production and wants work organised for collective benefit.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Not part of its political programme.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Intersectional views often oppose singling out minority religious expression; not discussed directly.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Black feminist activism addressed sexual violence and harassment, and Crenshaw's work shows how institutions marginalise women of colour.

social-market-economy.rationale: Reformist capitalism falls short of the Collective's goal of ending capitalism.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Anti-militarist but no stated demand to abolish armed forces.

rich-first.rationale: Equal distribution of resources contradicts allowing some to grow rich first.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutual credit banking is not discussed in the sources, so neutral.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Anti-imperialist and pro-redistribution stance suggests support; inferred.

property-franchise.rationale: Harper argued Black women needed the vote as protection; restricting votes by wealth contradicts the tradition.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Alice Walker's womanism links human solidarity and nature, but the sources do not state the ecofeminist thesis.

reification.rationale: Marx's analysis of economic relations is accepted but this concept is not discussed.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Anti-capitalist analysis of class power makes this plausible.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Rule-of-law formalities are not discussed in the sources, so neutral.

racial-franchise.rationale: Black feminists fought for suffrage for Black women; racial franchise is the opposite.

online-participation.rationale: Internet deliberation is not addressed by the sources, so neutral.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Randomly selected deliberative bodies are not discussed in the sources, though participatory politics is sympathetic; neutral.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Womanist and Black feminist religious thought reinterprets tradition, though not documented in the sources.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Davis co-founded Critical Resistance and calls for abolishing police and prisons, and Black feminist work ties incarceration to the criminalisation of Black women.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The Combahee socialist analysis ties freedom to ending class exploitation and redistributing resources, so concentrated wealth is seen as undermining liberation.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The Collective opposed heterosexism and many members were Black lesbians; military service is not discussed, so the answer follows from LGBT equality.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The Black church is a major tradition within the movement and womanist thought is often faith-based; state-promoted unbelief is inferred to be rejected.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Black feminism insists on inclusion of marginalised groups in power, which fits guaranteed shares, but constitutional design is not discussed.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Combahee socialism seeks collectively distributed resources and state-guaranteed services rather than reliance on private charity.

term-limits.rationale: The sources do not address term limits and adherents have no shared view.

vote-delegation.rationale: Electoral mechanics are not discussed; participatory aims could favour it, but nothing documents a position.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Emphasis falls on present, concrete injustices to Black women, so making extinction risk a top priority is inferred to rank lower.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Black feminism opposes sexism in every institution, so women's equal access to religious office is inferred; the sources do not address clergy.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The Collective's opposition to patriarchy and sexual politics makes male household authority incompatible with the movement.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Combahee's anti-racist, internationalist politics extends solidarity to immigrant and marginalised women; local voting rights for residents is inferred, not stated.

rent-control.rationale: Combahee's socialism and its attention to Black women's housing and poverty make rent caps a plausible inferred demand.

abolish-ip.rationale: Combahee is anti-capitalist, but it never discusses intellectual property; abolition is too radical for most adherents, so a mild disagree is inferred.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Combahee opposes militarism and state discipline; drilled national-service youth movements are inferred as contrary to its politics.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Combahee's anti-imperialism and anti-militarism imply opposition to nuclear weapons, though the Statement does not address basing.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Combahee's anti-imperialism implies opposition to foreign military bases; inferred, not stated.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Davis and the Black radical tradition call for recognising the crimes of slavery and racial violence; formal genocide recognition is inferred.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Combahee's socialism holds that resources should be distributed to those who create them, which favours rewarding work over ownership.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Davis defended armed self-defence by Black activists, so an absolute ban on killing in self-defence is not the mainstream view; inferred.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Collins treats identity as shaped by changing social conditions, so a claim of unbroken ancient national continuity is inferred as foreign to it.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Intersectionality holds that social categories are constructed through power, but the sources focus on gender and race rather than sex itself.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Intersectionality's founding point is that 'women' is not a single category because race and class cut across it.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Combahee's materialist politics does not centre martyr cults; inferred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Combahee analyses oppression through material and class relations; religious or spiritual struggle between good and evil is inferred as not its frame, though womanist strands differ.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Black feminism is internationalist and diasporic, but the sources do not discuss homeland-diaspora relations.

culture-before-state.rationale: Combahee puts concrete political and economic struggle ahead of cultural renewal; inferred.

god-not-male.rationale: Black religious feminist and womanist writers challenge exclusively male language for God, though the sources say little on it.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Black feminist and womanist theology judges tradition by its effect on Black women, but the sources do not state this directly.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Combahee's anti-racist politics rejects ethnic dominance of the economy; inferred from its stance against all interlocking oppressions.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Combahee does not claim peoples' territorial units; its anti-racist universalism makes this inferred as foreign.

independent-unions.rationale: Not discussed directly; the Combahee socialism and support for Black women workers' organising suggest labour bodies answerable to workers rather than to the state.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The Combahee Statement calls for socialist revolution in which work is organised for the collective benefit of those who do the work.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from Combahee socialism and its concern for health care and basic provision; local services are not discussed.

second-chamber.rationale: Legislative structure is not addressed and adherents have no common view.

municipal-property.rationale: Combahee favours collective control of production but never says whether it should be municipal.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Not addressed; Combahee organising was local and coalitional but sets out no confederal scheme.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from the critique of male-breadwinner norms; Black women have long worked for wages, so a wage framed around the worker's family is not the demand.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed; concern for health access is balanced by distrust of medical abuse of Black women.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not addressed by the sources and not a concern of the tradition.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not addressed; Davis's critique of surveillance and policing cuts against state tracing, but payments are not discussed.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from the tradition's opposition to state surveillance and policing of marginalised people.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred from Combahee's insistence on the dignity and self-determination of Black women and its opposition to state violence.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Collins treats spirituality as part of Black women's culture and knowledge, though the socialist strand is secular and religious womanist strands differ.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred: federal power has been the main protection against racist state governments, so revocable regional powers are the safer arrangement.

gm-crops.rationale: Not addressed; the tradition has no common view.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed; environmental justice is a concern but urban density is not.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Combahee holds that its politics come directly from its own identity and organises Black women around their specific interests.

racial-pride.rationale: Collins stresses self-definition and valuing Black women's own culture and knowledge, which makes racial pride legitimate.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred from the Combahee anti-imperialism and Davis's anti-militarism, which oppose aggressive wars.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Combahee's internationalism and anti-imperialism, which does not ground politics in nation-forming language.

communal-electorates.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the stress on shared multi-issue coalition politics over separate religious electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the anti-imperialist focus on US power rather than foreign plots against the country.

free-public-college.rationale: Combahee's socialism seeks resources shared with those who create them, and Black feminist work treats education as a route out of class exploitation.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred from the Combahee socialist strand, which favours public action and environmental justice over price instruments that burden poor communities.

future-generations.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the movement's liberation aims and environmental justice concerns.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Adherents split: Collins stresses Black women's distinct standpoint while others avoid essentialist claims about women's values.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred from Combahee's anti-imperialism and Davis's opposition to militarism and state violence.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the anti-imperialist and democratic stance against secret deals among states.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred from the Combahee socialist and anti-imperialist strand, which opposes unrestrained global capital; not addressed directly.

missingStatements.text: Police and prisons should be abolished and replaced with other ways of providing safety.
missingStatements.rationale: Davis co-founded Critical Resistance and calls for abolishing police and prisons, and Black feminist work ties incarceration to the criminalisation of Black women.

missingStatements.text: People should be protected from forced sterilisation and from state pressure to have or avoid having children.
missingStatements.rationale: Davis highlighted compulsory sterilisation of Black women, and Roberts showed that state policy criminalised Black pregnant women; Combahee worked on sterilisation abuse.
missingStatements.declined: Near-universal agreement against coerced sterilisation, so it fails the contested bar.

notes: Strands differ: the Combahee/Davis socialist strand is anti-capitalist while liberal Black feminists (Chisholm, Murray) are reformist, and positions on sex work, pornography and separatism are contested. Black lesbian feminists criticised white-led separatism.
